title: Public web and platform data collection
intro: Investigating public web and online-platform data structures, evaluating extraction approaches, and organizing collected information into documented datasets.
challenge: Public web interfaces are inconsistent. Useful information may appear in rendered pages, embedded JSON, or available API responses, with changes in page structure and missing fields requiring careful handling.
role: Built and tested Python-supported collection workflows; inspected web requests and data structures; prepared structured outputs and documented the approach, test cases, and edge cases.

approach.label: Inspect the source
approach.detail: Review public page structures, browser network activity, and available JSON or API responses before choosing an extraction approach.

approach.label: Collect deliberately
approach.detail: Use Python HTTP or browser-based workflows as appropriate to the source and task constraints.

approach.label: Shape the output
approach.detail: Transform collected fields into consistent tabular records suitable for downstream review.

approach.label: Document uncertainty
approach.detail: Record method assumptions, edge cases, and testing considerations rather than treating missing data as verified.

result: Prepared structured research outputs and reusable methodology documentation for downstream review and analysis. No confidential code, source records, or quantitative client outcomes are published here.

title: Regulated-industry account intelligence
intro: Converting industry-specific ICP requirements into defensible company and decision-maker research across energy, utilities, mining, infrastructure, and related regulated sectors.
challenge: Generic company directories rarely capture the full picture of regulated industries. Identifying relevant asset owners, regulators, projects, and responsible decision-makers requires combining specialized public sources with clear inclusion and exclusion rules.
role: Researched target accounts and professional roles; classified companies by sector and geography; added source notes, fit rationale, and review flags; organized segmented prospect lists.

approach.label: Translate the ICP
approach.detail: Define target industries, company types, geography, seniority, functions, and explicit exclusions.

approach.label: Map authoritative sources
approach.detail: Review company websites, agency and regulatory records, industry associations, and relevant event materials.

approach.label: Resolve account fit
approach.detail: Differentiate operating companies, regulators, advisors, and unrelated vendors; document the reasoning behind each classification.

approach.label: Prepare for activation
approach.detail: Structure target accounts and contacts with traceable sources, prioritization tiers, and fields suitable for enrichment or CRM review.

result: Produced organized, source-backed prospect research for targeting and review workflows. Client-specific names, datasets, outreach details, and performance metrics are not disclosed.

title: CRM-ready enrichment and data quality
intro: Turning incomplete or inconsistent account and contact research into standardized, source-backed files prepared for enrichment review and CRM import.
challenge: Records from websites, directories, event lists, and data vendors can conflict in naming, categorization, geography, or completeness. Uploading them without validation creates duplicates and uncertainty downstream.
role: Researched missing account attributes, standardized fields, flagged duplicate or uncertain records, and prepared HubSpot-ready import structures and Apollo enrichment inputs.

approach.label: Define a clear schema
approach.detail: Separate account fields, contact attributes, ICP classifications, and source/quality metadata.

approach.label: Normalize fields
approach.detail: Standardize company names, websites, geographic labels, role categories, and format conventions.

approach.label: Verify and flag
approach.detail: Cross-check source conflicts, identify candidate duplicates, and explicitly preserve unknown or unverified fields.

approach.label: Package handoffs
approach.detail: Organize CSV and Google Sheets outputs for review, enrichment, and HubSpot-compatible importing.

result: Delivered structured, reviewable data handoffs designed to make enrichment and CRM ingestion more reliable. Sample records shown elsewhere on this website are fictional demonstration data.

title: .NET and SQL reporting engineering
intro: Developing and maintaining data-intensive ASP.NET MVC application features, SQL Server reporting logic, and PDF/Excel exports governed by business rules.
challenge: Enterprise reporting must reconcile database queries, application filters, totals, date ranges, edge cases, and exported output. Differences across these layers can produce inconsistent user-facing results.
role: Developed and maintained C#/.NET features, SQL Server queries and stored procedures, dynamic UI behavior, and export workflows; investigated data discrepancies and bugs.

approach.label: Trace business logic
approach.detail: Understand how SQL queries, stored procedures, controller logic, and views contribute to a report or workflow.

approach.label: Implement application changes
approach.detail: Work across ASP.NET MVC, C#, Razor, JavaScript, jQuery, and SQL Server components.

approach.label: Align report outputs
approach.detail: Ensure PDF and Excel exports follow the same filter criteria, totals, dates, and business rules presented in the interface.

approach.label: Test real edge cases
approach.detail: Investigate grouped records, legacy data, account identifiers, overages, adjustments, and payment-related scenarios.

deliverables: SQL reporting logic and stored procedures
result: Maintained and improved data-heavy enterprise reporting workflows. Proprietary source code, application screenshots, and client records remain private.
